title: Chebiakinnausuk
summary: A Montauk North Neck boundary-mark name from the 1670 Wuchebesuck purchase, shown only as a general approximation.
why_this_matters: Chebiakinnausuk preserves boundary language from the 1670 Wuchebesuck purchase on Montauk's North Neck, with meanings such as marked separation or bound-mark. Its exact placement remains uncertain, but the name shows how boundaries could be named, marked, remembered, and later written into land agreements. Montaukett geography was a living framework of places and relationships, not simply lines imposed through colonial records.
introduction_content: Chebiakinnausuk, also written Chabiakinnauhsuk, is a Montauk North Neck placename recorded by Tooker as one of the bounds of the Wuchebesuck purchase.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Chebiakinnausuk and Chabiakinnauhsuk. The name is interpreted as the marked separation, where a boundary is marked, or a bound-mark.

Why Place Names Matter

“It is essential for our beautiful Elders to have an opportunity to record the true place names while they are still here with us, to preserve this information for future generations.”

— Rach McPhail, For past, present and future generations: Seeing First Nations place names in everyday life (2023), Direct quotation in article body
whereintheworld_content: Chebiakinnausuk preserves a Montaukett boundary term within a documented land transaction. Mapping it carefully as approximate keeps the place visible without claiming that the original marker has been found.
